## Texas Blackouts

```{r}
library(terra)
library(tmap)
library(tidyverse)
library(kableExtra)
library(sf)
library(stars)
```


```{r}
# Read in the data.
roads <- st_read("data/gis_osm_roads_free_1.gpkg.zip", query="SELECT * FROM gis_osm_roads_free_1 WHERE fclass='motorway'")
buildings <- st_read("data/gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1.gpkg.zip", query="SELECT *
FROM gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1
WHERE (type IS NULL AND name IS NULL)
OR type in ('residential', 'apartments', 'house', 'static_caravan', 'detached')")
texas51 <- rast("data/VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021038.h08v05.001.2021039064328.tif")
texas52 <- rast("data/VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021047.h08v05.001.2021048091106.tif")
texas61 <- rast("data/VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021038.h08v06.001.2021039064329.tif")
texas62 <- rast("data/VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021047.h08v06.001.2021048091105.tif")
```


```{r}
# Check CRS's.
# Both of the gpkgs are 4326
st_crs(roads)
st_crs(buildings)

# Also 4326
crs(texas51)
```


```{r}
# Check CRS's with a warning message. 
if(same.crs(texas51, roads)){
  print("CRS's match")
}else{(warning("CRS's do not match"))
}
```


```{r}
# Merge the rasters for the two days: 
feb7 <- merge(texas51, texas61)
feb16 <- merge(texas52, texas62)
```

```{r}
# Find the difference in light before and after the storm by subtracting the two rasters.
difference <- feb7 - feb16
```

```{r}
# Reclassify into 0s and 1s. 
rcl <- matrix(c(
   -Inf,   200,  NA,
   200,  Inf,  1
), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)

blackout <- as.factor(classify(difference, rcl = rcl))
```

```{r}
# Convert raster data to polygon vector data
blackout_poly <- as.polygons(blackout) |> 
  st_as_sf() |> 
  st_make_valid()
```

```{r}
# Create a bounding box to crop the blackout_poly vector. 
bbox <- st_bbox(c( xmin= -96.5, ymin=29, xmax=-94.5, ymax=30.5))
```

```{r}
# Crop the vector with the bounding box. 
cropped_blackout <- st_crop(blackout_poly, bbox)
```

```{r}
# Reproject the cropped_blackout to the CRS EPSG 3083.
cropped_blackout <- st_transform(cropped_blackout, crs= "EPSG:3083")
# Check to make sure the reprojecting worked. 
st_crs(cropped_blackout)
```

```{r}
# Change roads CRS to match the new blackout CRS. 
roads <- st_transform(roads, st_crs(cropped_blackout))


# Create a buffer of 200 meters from the roads
roadbuffer <- st_buffer(roads, dist = 200)
# Union the buffered areas. 
roadunion <- st_union(roadbuffer)



#Subtract the buffered road areas from the cropped_blackout data. 
blackoutnoroads <- st_difference(cropped_blackout,roadunion)

```

```{r}
# Identify where buildings overlap with blackouts 
# First, change the buildings CRS to match the cropped_blackout CRS. 
buildings <- st_transform(buildings, st_crs(cropped_blackout))
# Find where buildings overlap with blackouts
buildingblackout <- st_intersection(blackoutnoroads, buildings)
buildingpoints <- st_point_on_surface(buildingblackout)
```

```{r}
# Plot it!
tm_shape(buildingpoints)+
    tm_dots(fill='blue',fill_alpha=0.1)+
    tm_basemap("OpenStreetMap") +
    tm_scalebar() +
    tm_legend() +
    tm_title("Houson Homes Without Power After Feb 2021 Storms")
```

```{r}
# Count the number of rows in buildingpoints to see how many buildings are in the blackout. 
nrow(buildingpoints)
```

## 157,409 homes lost power after the storms. 




```{r}
## Find the Houston light intensity before and after the storms. 

# Crop feb7 to the Houston bounding box created earlier. 
feb7cropped  <- crop(feb7, ext(bbox))

# Plot the cropped feb7 raster.
beforestorm <- tm_shape(feb7cropped)+
    tm_raster(col.scale=tm_scale_continuous_log1p(values='viridis'),
    col.legend = tm_legend(title = "Radiance (W·sr−1·m−2)"))+
    tm_scalebar()+
    tm_title("Houston Light Intensity Before Feb 2021 Storms")

# Crop feb16 to the Houston bounding box created earlier. 
feb16cropped <- crop(feb16, ext(bbox))

afterstorm <- tm_shape(feb16cropped)+
    tm_raster(col.scale=tm_scale_continuous_log1p(values='viridis'),
    col.legend = tm_legend(title = "Radiance (W·sr−1·m−2)"))+
    tm_scalebar()+
    tm_title("Houston Light Intensity After Feb 2021 Storms")


tmap_arrange(beforestorm, afterstorm, nrow=1)
```

## The results of these two maps show that there is a significant decrease in light radiance coming from Houston after the February 2021 storms. This study provides a helpful visual overview, but there are other important variables missing for a more in depth analysis. For example, a future analysis could examine which neighborhoods in particular were most impacted, and how blackouts might be correllated with areas of a lower socioeconomic status.
